stages.title: Advanced linguistics and grammar
stages.hook: English adds -s, -ed and -ing. Mandarin adds almost nothing to its words. How does it still express tense, number and role?
explain: Linguists call Mandarin an analytic (or isolating) language: words have almost no inflection, so grammar is carried by word order, particles and function words (虚词, xūcí). The basic order is subject–verb–object, and modifiers come before what they modify, including whole relative clauses: 我昨天买的书 (the book I bought yesterday).

The smallest meaningful unit is the morpheme (语素, yǔsù). Most morphemes are one syllable (音节, yīnjié) and are written with one character, but modern Mandarin words are mostly two syllables. Tones are part of each syllable. Mandarin is also topic-prominent: 这本书我已经看过了 (this book, I have already read it) puts the topic first.

Complements (补语, bǔyǔ) add result, direction, degree or potential after a verb: 看完 (finish reading), 听得懂 (can understand by listening), 听不懂 (cannot). The potential complement is a feature without a direct English equivalent. Classifiers (量词) are obligatory in counting.
sentences: Word order is very important in Chinese.
Classifiers are a feature of Chinese.

gq.why: It is a negative potential complement: cannot understand by listening.

o: Little inflection, grammar via word order and particles
gq.why: Analytic languages use word order and particles rather than endings.

panel.q: In 这本书我已经看过了, what is 这本书?
panel.why: It is the topic, placed first, even though it is the object.

panel.q: Why is a single character not always a word in modern Mandarin?
o: Many words consist of two characters
panel.why: Most modern words are two syllables, made from two morphemes.

panel.q: Which is correct about relative clauses?
panel.why: Modifiers precede the noun: 我昨天买的书.

teach.model: Mandarin has almost no inflection, so word order and particles carry grammar. Words are formed from morphemes, mostly one syllable. Complements add result or possibility after verbs, and the topic often comes first.

trip.prompt: Find examples of analytic and synthetic languages and place Mandarin.

stages.title: Historical development of the language
stages.hook: The oldest known Chinese writing was scratched on turtle shells and bones over 3,000 years ago. How did it become today's script?
explain: The earliest mature Chinese writing is 甲骨文 (jiǎgǔwén), oracle bone script, from the late Shang dynasty (around 1250–1046 BCE). Later scripts include bronze inscriptions, 篆书 (zhuànshū, seal script), 隶书 (lìshū, clerical script) and 楷书 (kǎishū, regular script), which is the base of modern printing.

Spoken Chinese changed too. Linguists reconstruct Old Chinese and Middle Chinese (for example the rhyme books such as the Qieyun) by comparing varieties and poetry rhymes. Middle Chinese had an entering tone (入声) with final stops, which Cantonese still keeps and Mandarin has lost.

For two thousand years, formal writing used 文言文 (wényánwén, Literary Chinese), which differed from speech. The New Culture Movement and the May Fourth period (around 1919) promoted 白话文 (báihuàwén, vernacular writing). In the 1950s, mainland China adopted simplified characters.
stages.mnemonic: Bones, bronze, seal, clerical, regular: the script keeps evolving.
sentences: Oracle bone script is ancient writing.
Vernacular is closer to speech than Literary Chinese.
The shapes of characters keep evolving.

gq.q: Which script is the base of modern printed characters?
gq.why: Regular script (楷书) is the base of modern print.
It was the formal written language based on classical models.

panel.q: Why do linguists compare Cantonese and Mandarin when reconstructing Middle Chinese?
panel.why: Cantonese keeps final stops that Mandarin lost, providing evidence of older sounds.

panel.q: What changed around the May Fourth period?
panel.why: Writers promoted vernacular writing over Literary Chinese.

panel.q: Why is the date for 甲骨文 given as approximate?
panel.why: Dating relies on archaeology and the dynasty chronology, which has a margin of uncertainty.

teach.model: Chinese writing began with oracle bones about 3,000 years ago and evolved through seal, clerical and regular script. Literary Chinese differed from speech until vernacular writing spread in the early 20th century.

points.ask: What happened in the early 20th century?

trip.prompt: Look at an oracle bone image and compare one character with its modern form.

stages.title: Literature and cultural discourse
stages.hook: How did one short text, the Analects, shape ideas about education and society across East Asia?
explain: The 《论语》 (Lúnyǔ, Analects) records the sayings and conversations of Confucius (孔子) and his students. Its first line is 学而时习之，不亦说乎？ ("To learn and review it in due time, is that not a pleasure?"). Central ideas of Confucianism (儒家, Rújiā) include 仁 (rén, humaneness), 礼 (lǐ, ritual propriety) and 孝 (xiào, filial respect).

Daoism (道家, Dàojiā) is associated with 《道德经》 (Dàodéjīng) and emphasises following the natural way (道). 《诗经》 (Shījīng, Book of Songs) is the earliest collection of Chinese poetry. These texts are quoted in modern speech and writing, so cultural literacy means recognising such allusions.

Cultural discourse values are debated. Some scholars stress harmony and duty, others note critical and diverse voices in the tradition. Quotations are often shortened, so a reader must know the source. Interpretations of Confucian ideas have changed over time, and they are not one fixed doctrine.
stages.mnemonic: Learn, practise, enjoy: the Analects begins with study.
sentences: The Analects records the words and deeds of Confucius.
To learn and review in due time, is that not a pleasure?

gq.q: Which text is the earliest collection of Chinese poetry mentioned here?
gq.why: The Shijing is an early collection of songs and poems.

gq.q: Which concept is central in Confucianism?
gq.why: 仁 humaneness is a key virtue.

panel.q: Why is knowing the Analects part of cultural literacy?
o: It is often quoted and alluded to
panel.why: Many phrases and ideas are quoted or alluded to in everyday and written Chinese.

panel.q: Why is it misleading to treat Confucianism as one fixed doctrine?
panel.why: Interpretations changed over time and differ among thinkers.

panel.q: Which statement is balanced?
o: All scholars agree on one reading
It is a religion for everyone
panel.why: Scholars debate how much the tradition values harmony versus critique.

teach.model: The Analects, the Book of Songs and the Daodejing are classic texts. Confucianism stresses ideas such as 仁 and 礼, while Daoism stresses following the natural way. Knowing them helps readers recognise allusions.

points.ask: Why do these texts matter in modern language?

trip.prompt: Read the first chapter of the Analects in translation and compare the line quoted here.

stages.title: Advanced academic writing
stages.hook: What is the difference between a student essay and a research article? Structure and precision.
explain: A Chinese research article usually has a title, 摘要 (zhāiyào, abstract), 关键词 (guānjiàncí, keywords), an introduction, a 文献综述 (literature review), 研究方法 (research methods), results, discussion, conclusion and 参考文献 (references). The abstract summarises purpose, method and finding in a few sentences.

Strong academic prose is precise and hedged. Phrases such as 在一定程度上 (to a certain extent), 可能 (may) and 有待进一步研究 (needs further study) show caution. A section on 局限性 (júxiànxìng, limitations) is expected. Claims must be backed by 实证 (shízhèng, empirical) data or a clear 理论框架 (lǐlùn kuàngjià, theoretical framework).

Citation styles differ by field, and reference lists must be accurate and consistent. Avoid overly long sentences and vague claims, and keep the terminology stable throughout the paper. Peer review improves quality by finding weaknesses.
sentences: The method of this paper is a questionnaire survey.

gq.q: What goes in a 摘要?
o: A short summary of the paper
gq.why: An abstract briefly gives purpose, method and findings.

gq.q: What does 在一定程度上 do in a claim?
o: It strengthens it into a law
gq.why: It hedges, showing that the claim holds only to a degree.

panel.q: Why is a limitations section included?
o: To be honest about what the study cannot show
panel.why: It shows honesty about what the study cannot show.

panel.q: A paper claims a cause using a small survey with no controls. What is the best revision?
o: Hedge the claim and mention the limitation
panel.why: Hedge the claim and name the limitation.

panel.q: Why keep terminology stable throughout?
panel.why: Changing terms may suggest different concepts.

teach.model: A research article has an abstract, literature review, method, results, discussion, conclusion and references. Academic style is precise, careful and honest about limits.

points.ask: What parts does an article have?

trip.prompt: Compare the parts of a research article in Chinese and in English.

stages.title: Professional translation
stages.hook: Machine translation is fast. Why do professional translators still check every contract?
explain: Professional translation is a workflow: the client's brief, a 术语库 (shùyǔkù, termbase) and style guide (风格指南, fēnggé zhǐnán), translation, 校对 (jiàoduì, proofreading), and a review by a second linguist (审校, shěnjiào). Confidentiality (保密, bǎomì) is a professional duty.

本地化 (běndìhuà, localisation) goes beyond translation: it adapts units, date formats, names and cultural references for the target audience. 机器翻译 (jīqì fānyì, machine translation) is useful for drafts, and 译后编辑 (yìhòu biānjí, post-editing) means a human corrects the machine output. But errors in terms, tone or missing negatives can be serious.

When translating into Chinese, decide on simplified or traditional characters, and on terminology used in mainland China, Taiwan or Hong Kong, which may differ: for example "software" is 软件 on the mainland and 軟體 in Taiwan. Always check the target region.
sentences: Machine translation cannot fully replace human translators.

gq.why: A human edits the output of a machine translation.

gq.q: For which audience might the term 軟體 be appropriate?
gq.why: 軟體 is the term used in Taiwan, in traditional characters.

panel.q: Why is a termbase useful for a large project?
o: It removes the need for a brief
panel.why: It keeps terms consistent between translators and documents.

panel.q: A machine translation drops the word "not" in a safety instruction. What does this show?
o: It is only a style issue
panel.why: Dropped negatives can be dangerous, so human review is needed.

panel.q: What does localisation add beyond translation?
panel.why: It adapts format, units and cultural references for the audience.

teach.model: A translator follows a brief, uses a termbase, translates, then proofreads and has it reviewed. Localisation adapts content for the audience. Machine translation can help but needs human checking.

points.ask: What does a translator start with?

trip.prompt: Read about localisation and list two things that may need adapting.

stages.title: Interpretation of complex communication
stages.hook: A speaker says 这个想法很有意思 with a pause. A listener hears a refusal. How do we read what is meant?
explain: Pragmatics studies meaning in use. Chinese communication often prefers indirectness: 委婉 (wěiwǎn) means tactful or euphemistic and 含蓄 (hánxù) means implicit or reserved. Saying 有点困难 (a bit difficult) can mean it cannot be done.

客套话 (kètaohuà) are polite formulae, like 哪里哪里 (not at all) in reply to praise, or 改天请你吃饭 (let me treat you some other day), which may not be a firm plan. 面子 (miànzi, face) means public image and dignity, and speakers protect it by avoiding direct criticism.

反语 (fǎnyǔ, irony) means the opposite of the literal meaning. A reader must use context, tone, shared knowledge and relationship. These patterns vary with the person, the region, the generation and the situation, so generalisations are only tendencies, not rules for every speaker.
stages.mnemonic: Read the context, the relationship and the silence.
sentences: You need to hear the meaning behind the words.
The meaning of irony is opposite to its surface.

gq.q: What does 有点困难 often imply in a business reply?
o: It may mean it will not be done
gq.why: It can be a polite way of saying it is not feasible.
Polite formulae that are not always meant literally.

panel.q: A host says 改天请你吃饭. What is the sensible interpretation?
o: It may be only polite, unless a date is set
panel.why: It may be a polite closing, not a fixed plan.

panel.q: Why should we avoid saying "all Chinese speakers are indirect"?
o: Habits vary by person and setting
Because Chinese speakers are always direct
panel.why: Pragmatic habits vary by person, region and setting.

panel.q: Which clue helps decode irony?
panel.why: Context, tone and shared knowledge reveal the intended meaning.

teach.model: Chinese speakers often use indirect, tactful expressions and polite formulae. To interpret them, use context, tone and relationship. But these are tendencies, not rules for everybody.

trip.prompt: Find an example of indirectness in another language and compare.

stages.title: Language variation and dialectology
stages.hook: Are Cantonese and Mandarin dialects of one language, or two languages? Linguists say it depends on how you define the question.
explain: Dialectology (方言学, fāngyánxué) studies regional variation. Chinese varieties are often grouped as Mandarin (官话, Guānhuà), Wu (吴语), Yue or Cantonese (粤语), Min (闽语), Hakka (客家话), Xiang, Gan and others. They differ greatly in sounds and vocabulary, and speakers of different groups usually cannot understand each other without learning.

Mandarin has four tones, while Cantonese is usually described as having six contrasting tones in modern Jyutping, plus syllables ending in -p, -t and -k that continue the old entering tone (入声, rùshēng). In Taiwan, a phonetic system called 注音符号 (zhùyīn fúhào, Bopomofo) is used in schools alongside the Latin alphabet.

Calling them "dialects" (方言) reflects the shared writing and national identity, while many linguists call them separate languages based on mutual intelligibility (可懂度, kědǒngdù). People also code-switch (语码转换, yǔmǎ zhuǎnhuàn), using a local variety at home and Mandarin at school or work.
stages.mnemonic: Same script, different sounds; labels depend on the criteria.
sentences: Varieties often cannot understand each other.
He speaks a local variety at home and Mandarin at school.

gq.q: What feature of Middle Chinese does Cantonese keep?
o: Final stops of the entering tone
A phonetic system used in Taiwan
gq.why: It is a phonetic notation used in Taiwan.

panel.q: Why can one argue that Cantonese and Mandarin are separate languages?
panel.why: They have low mutual intelligibility.

panel.q: Why do many speakers still call them dialects?
o: They are spoken in one village
The label is a scientific rule
panel.why: Shared writing, history and national identity encourage the label.

panel.q: Which is an example of code-switching?
o: Local variety at home, Mandarin at work
panel.why: Changing variety depending on setting is code-switching.

teach.model: Chinese has groups such as Mandarin, Wu, Cantonese, Min and Hakka. They differ greatly in sound and vocabulary. Whether they are dialects or languages is debated, because writing and identity are shared but intelligibility is low.

trip.prompt: Look at the map of Chinese language groups and note where two groups meet.

stages.title: Specialised scientific or technical language
stages.hook: How do you say "cell", "atom" or "software" in Chinese when those ideas came from other languages?
explain: Scientific Chinese often creates new terms from existing characters, called calques or semantic translation. 电话 (diànhuà) is electric-speech, 火车 (huǒchē) is fire-vehicle, and 计算机 (jìsuànjī) is calculating machine. Others are coined as new characters, such as the names of chemical elements: 氧 (oxygen) and 氢 (hydrogen), with a radical for the state of matter.

Many modern terms were coined in Japan using kanji and then borrowed into Chinese, including 经济 (economy), 社会 (society) and 科学 (science). Others, like 细胞 (cell) and 基因 (gene), became standard in Chinese. 人工智能 (réngōng zhìnéng) is artificial intelligence, and 软件 (ruǎnjiàn) is software.

Technical writing is precise: units come with numbers (温度 wēndù, temperature), terms follow national standards, and one concept has one term. Some fields keep abbreviations from English, such as DNA or CPU, and variants exist between mainland China and Taiwan.
stages.mnemonic: New idea, old characters: 电 + 话.
sentences: The cell is the basic unit of living things.
An atom consists of a nucleus and electrons.

gq.q: What does 电话 literally mean?
gq.why: 电 is electricity and 话 is speech.
人工智能 is made of 人工 (artificial) and 智能 (intelligence).

panel.q: How was the word 经济 in modern Chinese commonly used?
o: Reused in Japan and borrowed back
panel.why: It was a term from classical Chinese reused in Japan and then borrowed back for "economy".

panel.q: Why do technical terms need standardisation?
o: So that each concept has one term
panel.why: One concept should have one clear term for accuracy.

panel.q: A report written for Taiwan uses 軟體. Why?
o: Because of local script and terminology
panel.why: Taiwan uses traditional characters and its own term.

teach.model: Scientific Chinese builds new terms from old characters, like 电话 and 计算机. Some terms came through Japan. Technical writing needs one term per concept, and terms can differ between mainland China and Taiwan.

trip.prompt: Find a Chinese term for a scientific idea and break it into its characters.

stages.title: Integrated proficiency project
stages.hook: You have learned sounds, characters, grammar and culture. How do you show what you can do and plan the next step?
explain: The integrated proficiency project combines reading, listening, speaking and writing around one topic, for example a presentation about a local issue with a summary, a short article and a recorded interview. 项目 (xiàngmù) means project, 汇报 (huìbào) report back, and 评估 (pínggū) assessment.

The international Chinese test 汉语水平考试 (HSK) measures proficiency in levels. A newer standard published in 2021 describes nine bands, and the speaking test is separate (HSKK). Alignments with CEFR levels are only approximate. A language portfolio can show real work: recordings, essays and corrections.

Reflection (反思, fǎnsī) is how you grow. Set a goal (目标, mùbiāo), measure progress (进步, jìnbù), find weaknesses such as tones or measure words, and plan practice: listening daily, writing weekly and conversation with native speakers.
sentences: My goal is to pass the Chinese proficiency test.
This project helped me make great progress.
I need to reflect on my study methods.

gq.why: HSK is a test of Mandarin proficiency for non-native speakers.

gq.q: What is the purpose of 反思?
gq.why: Reflection means thinking back to improve.

panel.q: Why is a portfolio useful?
o: It shows real work and progress
panel.why: It shows real samples of skill over time.

panel.q: A learner makes tone errors often. What is a sensible plan?
panel.why: Targeted practice with recordings and feedback addresses the weakness.

panel.q: Why is the CEFR alignment of HSK called approximate?
panel.why: The frameworks were designed differently, so correspondence is not exact.

teach.model: A final project combines reading, listening, speaking and writing. Tests such as HSK describe levels, and portfolios show real work. Reflect, set a goal and plan targeted practice.

trip.prompt: Read about the HSK levels and choose a realistic next goal.

sources: Common European Framework of Reference for Languages
